title: Permit reviews: 77% of first reviews missed the City’s own deadline

beats.text: How long should the first review of a building permit take?

visual.label: First review of a building permit

beats.text: The City’s own answer: 30 days.

visual.label: First review of a building permit

beats.text: Of 127,033 first reviews, 77 percent missed it.

visual.label: of 127,033 finished first reviews missed it, permits filed 2015 to 2026

beats.text: That’s the City’s own on-time flag, in its own published table.
The adding up is ours. This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Every desk misses most of the time.

visual.label: First reviews on time, by station

beats.text: Structural plan check met the deadline 17 percent of the time.

visual.label: First reviews on time, by station

beats.text: Building plan check, 19. Planning’s zoning check, 23. The best, 43.

visual.label: First reviews on time, by station

beats.text: Rechecks do better: of 88,730, 18 percent missed their 14-day deadline.
Missing three times in four isn’t an outlier. It’s how the process runs.

visual.line: Missing it three times in four is not an outlier; it is how the process runs.

beats.text: Then it changes.

visual.label: First reviews on time, by year filed

beats.text: Permits filed in 2021: 11 percent on time. In 2025: 73 percent.

visual.label: First reviews on time, by year filed

beats.text: Part of it is counting: recent years include only reviews already finished.

visual.line: Recent years include only reviews that have already finished, which flatters them.

beats.text: The table doesn’t say what changed.

visual.line: Recent years include only reviews that have already finished, which flatters them.

beats.text: Do paid permit consultants buy speed? 2,269 scored permits list one.

visual.label: Permit consultants and expediters
visual.kicker: A check that comes back clean

beats.text: Their average place among like reviews: 0.50.
Without one: 0.50. No faster.
131 firms and professionals appear on 40 or more jobs.

visual.label: firms and professionals on 40 or more scored jobs
visual.sub: 7 faster than like reviews beyond chance; 7 slower

beats.text: 7 are faster beyond chance, and 7 slower.

visual.label: firms and professionals on 40 or more scored jobs
visual.sub: 7 faster than like reviews beyond chance; 7 slower

beats.text: The fastest, a contractor, finished 26 percent of its review visits the day they arrived.

visual.label: Comstock Crosser & Assoc Develp Co Inc.

beats.text: Of 18 faster firms, 8 also appear as a lobbyist, client, donor, or commissioner’s business.

visual.label: Clear Channel Outdoor
visual.kicker: 8 of 18 faster firms appear in other records

beats.text: At hearings, one firm, Reuben, Junius and Rose,

visual.label: of 75 hearing items presented by a registered lobbyist or permit consultant

beats.text: presented 49 of 75 items led by registered lobbyists.

visual.label: of 75 hearing items presented by a registered lobbyist or permit consultant

beats.text: Their items were changed or disapproved more often, not less: 31 percent against 22.7.
Speed has honest causes: complete drawings, simple repeat work.

visual.line: Faster reviews have honest causes: complete drawings, simple repeat work.

beats.text: And nothing on record ties any review to any contact.

visual.line: Faster reviews have honest causes: complete drawings, simple repeat work.

beats.text: And the code? 10 rules were found and quoted.
